title: Maximum Overlapping Intervals
statement:
You are given `n` closed intervals `[start[i], end[i]]` with integer endpoints and `start[i] ≤ end[i]`. Two intervals **overlap** if they share at least one point, so intervals that merely touch at an endpoint (for example `[1, 4]` and `[4, 8]`) do overlap. This is the same rule as for trains: a train that arrives at the exact moment another one departs still needs a platform of its own.

Find the largest number of intervals that all contain one common point. Print that number.

This is the core of problems such as the minimum number of railway platforms needed for a timetable, or the minimum number of servers/rooms needed so that no two overlapping jobs share one.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains two integers `start[i]` and `end[i]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum number of intervals containing a common point.

examples.explanation: The point 4 lies in [1,4], [2,6] and [4,8]. The interval [9,10] overlaps none of them.
The intervals are pairwise disjoint, so no point belongs to more than one interval.
The point 5 is in [5,5], [5,5] and [1,10]. The point 7 is in [1,10], [6,7] and [7,9]. Neither point is in four intervals.

hints: The maximum overlap is always reached at the start point of some interval, so you only need to examine O(n) candidate points.
Turn every interval into two events: a start at `start[i]` and an end at `end[i]`. Sort the events by coordinate and sweep, keeping a running count of open intervals.
At equal coordinates, process starts before ends, because intervals are closed and touching endpoints overlap.
